correctness.rationale: The formula follows correctly from the known classification and standard counting. Tóth–Waldhauser's Theorem 4.7 identifies the polymorphism-homogeneous finite abelian groups exactly as those with homocyclic Sylow subgroups. A homocyclic group of order \(p^a\) is \((\mathbb Z/p^{a/m}\mathbb Z)^m\) for a divisor \(m\mid a\), and its automorphism group is the corresponding general linear group over \(\mathbb Z/p^{a/m}\mathbb Z\), giving the stated reciprocal mass. Dividing by the classical Hall–Cohen–Lenstra exact-order reciprocal-automorphism mass yields the displayed density. The \(m=1\) term is the finite product tending to the claimed infinite product, while every other divisor contributes at most an exponentially small remainder. Sylow factorization gives the general-order product.
